summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — LMT +11%, ALLE +10%, URI +10%, TMO +9%, DGX +9%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (TSLA -15%, TMUS -11%, ROL -9%, DOV -8%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: TSLA (-14.52%) — Q2 2026 EPS $0.33 missed $0.53 est. (record $28.2B revenue) as capex/AI-robotics spend surged 142%, crushing margins; multiple analysts cut price targets over following days. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — likely excluded by an earnings-blackout filter that drops mega-cap names in the days around a scheduled print (earnings hit 7/22), so the bot had no live signal for the multi-day post-earnings slide into 7/24.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 EPS $7.94 vs ~$7.09 est, revenue +11% YoY to $20.1B, record $230B backlog, raised FY26 guidance
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — LMT is a large-cap defense/aerospace industrial, a sector/category the bot's tradable universe doesn't cover; the earnings gap was also pre-market driven, favoring pre-open positioning over intraday signals.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap defense/aerospace (e.g. LMT, RTX, NOC, GD) to the universe, or add an earnings-gate that admits names with pre-market gap ≥8% and guidance raise on report day regardless of prior sector inclusion.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 2026 beat: revenue +12.7% YoY, EPS $2.40 (+17.6% YoY) topped estimates; raised FY26 adjusted EPS guide to $8.85-$9.00
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ALLE is a ~$15B industrials/building-products name, a sector/cap bucket the bot's momentum and news-reactive strategies don't currently scan, so the premarket earnings gap was never evaluated.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an earnings-day universe override: scan all NYSE/NASDAQ names (not just core sector universe) for premarket gap >=8% on reported EPS/revenue beat + raised guidance, and route qualifiers into the earnings-gate strategy regardless of static sector inclusion.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 2026 EPS $12.76 vs $11.59 est, revenue $4.41B vs $4.21B est; raised FY26 revenue guide to $17.5-17.8B and EBITDA guide by $300M
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — URI is a mega-cap industrial/equipment-rental name trading near $1,140/share, likely excluded by a max-share-price or sector (construction/industrials) filter rather than a technical signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a per-share-price cap override (or switch sizing to notional/fractional shares) so triple-digit-to-four-digit priced large-caps like URI aren't structurally excluded from the universe purely on nominal price.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 2026 earnings beat (EPS $6.03 vs est., revenue +10% to $11.99B) plus raised FY26 guidance to $47.4-48.1B, reported pre-market 7/23.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — TMO is a large-cap, low-beta life-sciences/lab-instruments name that momentum/mean-reversion universes built around higher-volatility sectors typically screen out entirely.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an earnings-gate override that admits any S&P 500 name posting a post-results gap ≥7% within the first 30min of trading, even if outside the strategy's default sector/beta universe filter.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 EPS $3.12 vs $2.85 est, revenue +10.2% YoY; raised FY26 EPS/revenue guidance; NY cleared Haystack MRD test for all 50 states
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — DGX is a large-cap diagnostics/healthcare-services name, a sector/cap bucket the bot's tradable universe doesn't cover, so no filter ever got a chance to evaluate the earnings gap.
top_movers.suggestion: Expand universe inclusion criteria to add healthcare-services large-caps (or a market-cap/sector screen sweep) so an earnings-gate can catch post-earnings gaps like this one even though it's not a typical momentum-sector name.

top_movers.catalyst: Rebound rally continuing from the Jul 21 post-earnings selloff — investors reassessed the biotech guidance cut (delayed chromatography-resin shipments) as timing, not demand, weakness.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — DHR is a mega-cap ($150B+) diagnostics/life-sciences conglomerate, a sector/cap bucket the bot doesn't track; also this was a multi-day post-earnings-drift recovery, not a same-day gap a scanner would catch.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings-drift screen that admits any-sector large caps showing ≥5% 3-day recovery after a >10% post-earnings drop, bypassing the standard universe filter for a short event window.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 2026 EPS $0.33 missed $0.53 est. (record $28.2B revenue) as capex/AI-robotics spend surged 142%, crushing margins; multiple analysts cut price targets over following days.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — likely excluded by an earnings-blackout filter that drops mega-cap names in the days around a scheduled print (earnings hit 7/22), so the bot had no live signal for the multi-day post-earnings slide into 7/24.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a post-earnings re-entry rule: names removed by the earnings-blackout filter re-enter the universe T+1 after release if the post-print gap/drift exceeds ±5%, so the bot can catch delayed selloffs like this one.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 EPS beat ($2.85 vs $2.58 est) but revenue missed ($22.79B vs $22.98B) and management guided to slower Q3 subscriber growth on churn risk from pricier plans.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — TMUS is a mega-cap, low-beta telecom typically screened out of momentum/small-cap universes; even if watched, this was a guidance-driven post-earnings gap that pre-market positioning would need to catch, not an intraday signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a large-cap earnings-reaction watchlist (S&P 500 telecom/staples) with a rule to flag next-day entries when post-earnings gap ≥8% is driven by forward guidance cuts, independent of the momentum universe's small/mid-cap filters.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 2026 EPS $0.32 missed $0.34 est. and revenue $1.08B missed $1.10B est.; slower Orkin residential pest-control demand growth.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ROL is a steady, low-beta specialty consumer-services/pest-control name, a sector/vol profile momentum and mean-reversion universes typically screen out in favor of higher-beta, higher-volume tickers.
top_movers.suggestion: Add an earnings-gap scanner that pulls any ticker (regardless of static universe membership) with an after-hours/pre-market gap ≥7% on an earnings date into a watchlist for next-day open evaluation.

top_movers.catalyst: Q2 EPS ($2.74) roughly in line/slight miss and revenue ($2.19B) missed estimates; facility-consolidation/labor issues cut organic growth ~1-1.5pts, overshadowing raised FY26 guidance and 16% bookings growth — stock fell ~8-10%.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — DOV is a large-cap diversified industrial conglomerate (multi-segment: refrigeration, pumps, aerospace/defense, biopharma), a sector/cap bucket the bot's current strategies don't cover at all.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a diversified-industrials/large-cap sector bucket (mkt cap >$15B, S&P 500 members) with an earnings-day gap scanner that flags post-results moves ≥5% for next-day mean-reversion or momentum follow-through entries.
